meta.note: R15.2 quiz contract: items[].{id,nodeId,prompt,options[{text,explain}],correct,sourceRef}. Authored from page content only — never invent values the page doesn't support.

items.prompt: Why divide QKᵀ by √dₖ before the softmax?

options.text: To normalize the output vectors to unit length
options.explain: No — the output is a weighted sum of V rows; its length isn't normalized by the scaling.

options.text: To keep large dot products from saturating the softmax
options.explain: Yes — as dₖ grows, dot products grow in variance; unscaled, softmax pins near one-hot and gradients vanish. The viz's √dₖ toggle shows exactly this.

options.text: To reduce the computational cost of the matmul
options.explain: No — the division is elementwise and adds (tiny) cost; it changes numerics, not complexity.

options.text: To make the attention weights sum to 1
options.explain: No — softmax alone guarantees weights sum to 1, with or without scaling.

items.prompt: In Attention(Q,K,V), what does the softmax produce?

options.text: Relevance weights over the keys that sum to 1
options.explain: Yes — each query row becomes a distribution over keys; those weights then mix the V rows.

options.text: New value vectors to replace V
options.explain: No — V is untouched; softmax output only decides how much of each V row to blend.

options.text: A probability distribution over the vocabulary
options.explain: No — vocabulary distributions come from the final output layer, not attention.

items.prompt: With no scaling, what happens to query·key dot products as dₖ grows?

options.text: Their variance grows with dₖ, pushing softmax toward saturation
options.explain: Yes — a sum of dₖ independent products grows in variance ~dₖ; that's the failure the √dₖ factor undoes. Try dₖ=64 with scaling off in the viz.

options.text: They stay in the same range regardless of dₖ
options.explain: No — each extra dimension adds another term to the sum; the spread grows.
No — the opposite: more terms means larger typical magnitude.

items.prompt: Softmax as a "relevance dial" means keys similar to the query receive…

options.explain: Yes — higher query–key similarity → higher score → larger share of the (fixed) attention budget.
No — equal shares only happen when all scores tie (or temperature → ∞).

options.text: Attention proportional to their position in the sequence
options.explain: No — position enters through positional encodings, not through the softmax itself.
